target_architecture: One coherent logical database with compact shared authoritative state and selectively activated exact physical/execution experts. Make ordinary state implicit where useful, represent sparse deviations, and choose durable, reconstructable or ephemeral lifetimes by measured whole-system cost. Seek joint speed, CPU and memory improvements rather than separate full specialist copies.
architecture_integration_boundary: The native library exports shared storage and transactions with selectable legacy AVL and experimental packed-page formats. Packed base pages and bounded deltas serve point, scan and transaction paths under the same snapshot, validation and publication machinery. This integrates a physical representation, not automatic mixture-of-experts routing. Factorization, certificates and other typed query mechanisms remain in the separate historical executable. Implicit extent mapping, fine version reuse, cost-aware expert lifetimes and resource governance remain incomplete.
next_integration: Attribute baseline costs using phase CPU, I/O calls/bytes, allocations and publication timing. Existing elapsed-time trials do not establish CPU or RSS improvements.
Integrate scan-friendly arbitrary-key pages, fixed-extent implicit mapping and bounded sparse updates under the same logical transaction and recovery API, retaining the AVL control.
Specify expert semantic eligibility, snapshot coverage, state lifetime and admission/retirement cost. Reject stale or incomplete expert coverage rather than filter only existing candidates.
Connect eligible research mechanisms through shared state with explicit typed query/update contracts where required. Do not infer arithmetic semantics from arbitrary binary values.

Measure full lifecycle resource vectors and no-expert fallback overhead, with predeclared tolerances, uncertainty and adversarial workload shifts. No universal superiority claim without matched specialist evidence.

value_cache_boundary: Disabled by default. Point reads alone admit values up to 4096 bytes and capacity-plus-metadata charge up to one eighth of the shared budget. Scans and compaction do not admit values. The committed-source trials support repeated-key reuse, not a general speedup. The reported 0.4-microsecond per-call median is below the lab's 1-microsecond reporting threshold and does not support a precise latency ratio. Unique reads and scans show no consistent benefit; 1 KiB-cache trials admit no values and show overhead. FIFO point admission may waste work or evict nodes under one-touch traffic. Cache charge and container capacities are not allocated-byte/RSS guarantees. No file format or durability barrier changes.
compaction_boundary: Preparation and data sync run outside the foreground state mutex. Publication still acquires it and syncs the manifest. Compaction and collection serialize through a maintenance lock. Any intervening commit invalidates the candidate, requiring explicit retry. No foreground latency bound, bounded retry cost, or bandwidth isolation is established.
grouped_update_boundary: Disabled by default. Empty-tree insert batches and replacement-only batches may share immutable ancestors. Deletes, mixed structural batches, single-key writes, oversized scratch batches and allocation failure use the proven sequential path. Temporary borrowed-entry references are capped at 64 KiB and one eighth of transaction_bytes, separately from staging charge. Bulk construction changes tree topology and serialized bytes. Replacement-only batches preserve topology, publication barriers and logical revisions. Correctness regressions and all 18 committed-source campaign trials passed. Median update-phase arena bytes fell 51% and total pre-maintenance arena bytes fell 14%. Normal-cache update time fell from 101.97 to 87.29 ms, and 1 KiB update time fell from 174.38 to 164.42 ms. Normal-cache load and single-row mutations were nearly unchanged, and ranges regressed slightly. SQLite remained faster. The result supports opt-in use only, not a general speedup or production-readiness claim. See results/spi/grouped-normal-committed-v1/summary.json and results/spi/grouped-small-committed-v1/summary.json. Arena counters exclude manifests and measure application-written bytes, not device write amplification.
packed_storage_boundary: Experimental and disabled by default. Create with packed_pages=true or use spi-packed. SPIMETA2 persists the format, older readers reject it, and current readers select the persisted format on open without conversion. Sorted base payloads are at most 16 KiB, values above 1 KiB use overflow records, and deltas are capped at eight records and 4 KiB cumulative payload. A fence AVL locates pages rather than individual rows. Point reads use validated serialized bytes and offsets, scans merge bounded lineages, and splits stream staged writes. Page/node/value caches share one charged budget. Scans do not admit pages, and retirement releases page containers. Temporary decoded pages, staging, output and allocator overhead are not included in that cache charge. Empty interior fence pages persist through compaction. No fixed-extent mapper, fine slot reuse, automatic workload routing or global RAM bound is claimed. All 33 source-identified normal, 1 KiB and 4 KiB-value campaign trials passed complete-output and cache contracts. At 8 MiB/64-byte values, packed full scans fell 15.54 to 1.33 ms, load fell 163.12 to 78.06 ms, unique reads fell 15.97 to 1.77 ms, and application-written arena bytes fell 2,585,984 to 495,120. At 1 KiB, packed point median regressed 46.6 to 86.7 microseconds and updates 150.66 to 186.97 ms. At 4 KiB values, ranges regressed 2.38 to 2.66 ms. SQLite remained faster on general scans, ranges, updates and durable commits. These results support packed storage as an opt-in workload-specific expert, not a default or general superiority claim. Diagnostic attribution of packed cache misses and further CPU/memory optimization remain open.
packed_profile_attribution: The original 21 packed-profile trials and 12 additional one-seed paired diagnostic trials passed output/contracts. In the additional 1 KiB packed warm-read phase, both CRC builds requested about 34.72 MB of Rust allocations and read 32.61 MB. Bitwise instrumented checksum time was 143.27 ms of a 173.89 ms phase, versus slicing-by-eight 16.69 ms of a 41.40 ms phase. Sampled process CPU was 171.875 versus 31.25 ms, includes harness/instrumentation and has coarse OS resolution. This supports targeted compute savings, not a precise general CPU/op claim. CRC tables add 8 KiB static read-only data. Page-miss read bytes and allocation amplification remain. See results/spi/packed-crc-profile-bitwise-small-v1 and results/spi/packed-crc-profile-slicing-small-v1.
direct_scan_boundary: Direct packed-base scans seek validated offsets before allocating rows and move owned inline Snapshot outputs. Delta chains retain bounded materialization without a second head read. Generation, CRC, cache admission, output-budget and publication contracts are unchanged. The spi-scan-materialized build preserves an explicit same-source control. All 54 paired release trials and 18 persistent-file comparisons passed. With normal cache, packed direct versus materialized medians were 0.398 versus 0.539 ms for full scans, 0.724 versus 1.005 ms after mutations, and 22.6 versus 41.8 microseconds for ranges. At 1 KiB, full scans were 0.432 versus 0.565 ms, but updates increased from 116.98 to 122.56 ms and maintenance from 18.37 to 20.84 ms. Unchanged engine controls also varied. Three seeds do not prove causal regressions, statistical equivalence or an across-workload win. See results/spi/packed-direct-scan-paired-v1/summary.json.
delta_view_boundary: Experimental direct-delta packed scans merge validated four-byte row references across the bounded immutable lineage. Newer rows replace older handles and tombstones remove them. The full visible page-size bound is retained. Private tests compare materialized/direct output, reads, generation checks, pinned snapshots, overflow ownership and malformed limits. The three-mode campaign is pending. Temporary record Arcs, references and returned output buffers are not total-RSS bounds. No point/write/compaction algorithm change or automatic router is claimed.
diagnostic_boundary: The spi-profile build and native-profile campaigns are attribution-only. Normal scan median attribution was 8,000 reads, 352,000 bytes and 4,000 checksums per full scan. Tiny-cache load added about 77,000 reads. Phase wall/CPU includes instrumentation and harness work. Rust allocation counts exclude SQLite/native allocations, process memory is process-wide, and nested timers overlap. No timing or CPU speedup claim is based on diagnostic runs.
benchmark_boundary: Same local binary-key operation stream is not equivalent full database semantics. Cache-cleared API calls are not device-cold reads. Single-row mutation tests must actually change the stored value. Keep old benchmark schemas as historical evidence only.
historical_lab: Existing kernel results and known ranking/numeric defects are separate from this new storage baseline. A passing lab test does not establish arbitrary-input correctness or validate this engine.
crc_paired_boundary: All 54 paired release trials and 18 post-maintenance persistent-file comparisons passed from identical source bytes. At 1 KiB, packed points fell 92.3 to 22.5 microseconds, unique reads 163.45 to 29.90 ms and updates 200.12 to 125.79 ms. Normal packed scans fell 1.456 to 0.615 ms, close to SQLite's 0.617 ms in that arm. Large-value packed ranges fell 2.60 to 0.80 ms. Normal packed updates increased 85.33 to 87.11 ms and large-value single commits 9.36 to 9.53 ms. SQLite controls varied too, so small changes are not causal evidence. SQLite remains faster on general updates, durable commits and most ranges. Three seeds do not establish statistical equivalence, service latency or total-resource dominance. CRC accelerates compute without reducing page-miss bytes or allocation volume. See results/spi/packed-crc-paired-v1/summary.json. All experimental storage options remain disabled by default.
direct_scan_allocation_boundary: All 18 diagnostic trials passed output, source and implementation contracts. One seed per mode and cache/value regime was measured. Normal packed full-scan Rust allocation requests fell from 783408 to 543408 bytes (31%) and calls from 6094 to 4082. Normal range allocation requests fell from 2664592 to 1772504 bytes. The 1 KiB full-scan requests were the same as normal-cache requests in both modes; post-mutation requests fell from 1360700 to 1215900 bytes. For 4 KiB values, full-scan requests fell only from 4294624 to 4238624 bytes; post-mutation requests were unchanged. Corresponding scan/range read calls and bytes matched exactly between modes. These are allocation requests including harness work, not retained memory, process RSS or native SQLite allocation totals. CPU samples were too coarse for short phases. Delta materialization, transaction output assembly and packed page-miss read amplification remain. See results/spi/packed-direct-profile-direct-base-normal-v1/summary.json and the corresponding materialized, small and large control directories.
